thread:
matthew: hitting a nasty one during the new hire notebook walkthrough — AsyncClient constructor blows up with RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop
elaine: ugh. notebook environment again. can you paste the tiny repro?
matthew: super tiny:
```python
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(api_key="fake")  # fails on init
await client.generate("hey")
```
sam: that usually means the ctor is doing blocking auth and calling asyncio.run under the hood
matthew: stack (trimmed):
```
RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/async_client.py", line 79, in __init__
    token = self._sync_get_token()
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/async_client.py", line 112, in _sync_get_token
    asyncio.run(self._refresh_token())
```
ashley: yikes. i've seen this pattern in an old sample app — ctor doing network work + using asyncio.run. total footgun for notebooks, uvicorn, pytest-asyncio tests
mike: long-term fix: constructors should never call network or loop-creating utilities. offer an async factory and a sync convenience wrapper instead
elaine: agreed. workaround for now: use nest_asyncio in the notebook (not ideal):
```python
import nest_asyncio
nest_asyncio.apply()
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(api_key="fake")
await client.generate("hey")
```
elsie: Q: why not have __init__ accept an already minted token so imports are cheap?
sam: good idea — __init__(token=...) to skip auth. but we still need a clear public async factory for common flows
mike: proposed API changes:
- make __init__ purely local: store args, no IO
- add `@classmethod async def create(cls, *, api_key=None, token=None, base_url=None):` which performs async auth and returns client
- add `def from_api_key_sync(...)` for sync users (uses requests, blocking but explicit)
- support `async with client:` context to close background tasks
ashley: also update notebook quickstart and sample-app to call `client = await AsyncClient.create(api_key=...)` and show the sync shim in a separate cell for sync users
matthew: small nit: name the factory `create` or `open`? `create` reads clearer to me that it's a coroutine
sam: +1 for `create` — `init` is confusing
mike: implementation notes for eng: move token refresh logic into async-only flows, add DeprecationWarning on old ctor if it still triggers IO, add a linter/test that runs the sample notebooks under pytest-asyncio to catch regressions
infra-bot: issue created: DEVEX-2147 — "AsyncClient ctor performs blocking auth; add AsyncClient.create and lazy init" (assigned to @mike) :white_check_mark:
elsie: i'll send a docs PR to the quickstart showing both patterns and explicitly call out "don't perform network calls at import time in notebooks or app module scope"
matthew: thanks — this was blocking a hiring setup so glad it's triaged quickly :thumbsup:
mike: i'll pick up DEVEX-2147, draft the change, and put a short migration note in the changelog. planning to ship a patch release next week
ashley: i'll push the sample-app notebook update and link the PR to the issue
elaine: also can we add a CI check that imports our sample apps inside a real Jupyter kernel to prevent docs regressions? helps catch these import-time IO issues early
mike: good idea. i'll add a small end-to-end smoke job in CI to execute the quickstart notebook (no heavy assertions, just ensure imports and factory usage don't crash)
matthew: awesome, thanks everyone
